DataFinder provides you with a server level \- Java SDK to simplify the complexity of server level event tracking. By using the SDK, you can focus solely on the event tracking scheme and not on specific reporting details. This article shows you an example of the integrated flow and event tracking configuration of the Java SDK.

<span id="913e9dcb"></span>

# Preparation

<span id="68d545de"></span>
## Step 1 (optional): Create event tracking requirements/Enter custom event tracking

After completing the event tracking planning, it is recommended that you create the event tracking requirements according to the planning and then enter the custom event tracking into the DataFinder to complete the warehousing of the custom event tracking in the DataFinder metadata.


* Event tracking request management: You can manage event tracking requirements through DataFinder's event tracking request management function, and you can continue to maintain and manage requirements in the event tracking request management page to improve management efficiency. See the operation to create event tracking request management [Request Management](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Request_Management).

* Custom event tracking entry: You can first create custom event tracking metadata into the DataFinder according to the event tracking plan. For activity details, see [New event](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/General_Events#_2-1-%E6%96%B0%E5%A2%9E%E4%BA%8B%E4%BB%B6), [Add event properties](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Event_Properties#_2-1-%E6%96%B0%E5%A2%9E%E4%BA%8B%E4%BB%B6%E5%B1%9E%E6%80%A7), [Add user properties](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/User_Properties#533b53ea).


<span id="ff82f708"></span>
## Step 2: Get the APPID/APP Key

Before SDK integration, you need to obtain the application ID (APPID or APP Key) generated by DataFinder when creating an application on DataFinder for subsequent SDK integration configuration.


* In the SaaS\-cloud native scenario, you can find the corresponding application in "Project Center" \> "Project Management" \> "Project Details", click "Access Data", and view the application ID (APPID) and APP URL of the application in the application details. For details, please refer to [Project Management](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Project_Management__).

   <span>![图片](https://p9-arcosite.byteimg.com/tos-cn-i-goo7wpa0wc/c52873d5e5ef4d7da390c4c102215d88~tplv-goo7wpa0wc-image.image) </span>

* Privatization scenario, same as SaaS\-cloud native scenario


<span id="ed652ecc"></span>
## Step 3: Obtain the data upload address

When reporting data access, you need to confirm your data reporting address according to the current environment type and terminal type. If the reporting address is set incorrectly, you will not be able to check the reported data in the future.

<div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="warning" data-tips-is-title="true">warning</div>



* <div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="warning">Please confirm the type of environment you are currently using before reporting data, and configure the reporting address according to the type of environment. To view the current environment type see <a href="https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/SaaS_Cloud-Native_Privatized_Environments">SaaS Cloud\-Native & Privatized Environments</a>.</div>


* <div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="warning">If you are using a SaaS\-cloud native environment, you also need to confirm the region where your service is located, and report the address according to the region configuration (usually your service will be in Southeast Asia \- Johor region, and some users may use other regions). SaaS\-cloud native users see the region where the service is located <a href="https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Supported_Regions">Supported Regions</a>.</div>

# Integrated SDK

<span id="cb6b1a28"></span>
## Understand the reporting model

The Growth Analytics SDK supports multiple reporting modes: HTTP, KAFKA, and you can choose to use the appropriate mode on demand. The comparison is as follows.


|**Comparison term** |**HTTP mode** |**KAFKA mode** |
|---|---|---|
|Supported environment types |* SaaS\-cloud\-native<br><br>* privatization |* Privatization support only |
|deployment complexity |simple |simple |
|reliability |high |very high |
|performance reporting |High, support batch reporting. |high |
|version requirement |* SDK \> = 1.5.7 Version |* SDK \> = 1.5.7 Version<br><br>* Privatization version 4.1 (inclusive) is now supported. |
|applicable scenario |* Most scenarios can be used, and if the cross\-network latency is relatively high, the batch mode can be used (all environments support it).<br><br>* You can refer to the section "Best Practices" \-\- \> "Viewing Reporting Delays" to view reporting delays. |This pattern is recommended when the service and finder of the integrated SDK are on the same network. |
|summarize |* The same network recommends using KAFKA mode for reporting<br><br>* Other scenarios recommend using HTTP ||

<span id="d90921e2"></span>
## Step1: Add dependencies

<span id="1c4394fb"></span>
### Get the latest version of the SDK

It is recommended that you integrate the latest version of the SDK. The current SDK is open source, you can go to the Git repository to get the latest version of the SDK: [github open source repository](https://github.com/volcengine/datarangers-sdk-java).

<span id="b3e801a0"></span>
### Add dependency method 1: maven dependency

You need to configure the BytePlus repository address in maven's settings first:

```XML
<repositories>
  <repository>
    <id>bytedance-volcengine</id>
    <name>bytedance Volcengine</name>
    <url>https://artifact.bytedance.com/repository/Volcengine/</url>
  </repository>
</repositories>
```


<div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="tip" data-tips-is-title="true">tip</div>



* <div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="tip">The above url: <code>https://artifact.bytedance.com/repository/Volcengine/</code>can be used directly for maven configuration, and does not support direct browser open access.</div>


* <div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="tip">If you wish to view the full repository through a browser, use your browser to open the url containing the subdirectories: <code>https://artifact.bytedance.com/repository/Volcengine/com/datarangers/</code>.</div>



Then you can configure the dependencies normally:

```XML
<dependency>

  <groupId>com.datarangers</groupId>

  <artifactId>datarangers-sdk-core</artifactId>
  
//latest version is recommended, configuration example: 1.5.13-release.(Note that -release is part of the verison name)
  <version>{version}</version>

</dependency>
```


We provide a packaged starter package that you can import in pom as follows:

```XML
<dependency>

   <groupId>com.datarangers</groupId>

   <artifactId>datarangers-sdk-starter</artifactId>

   //latest version is recommended, configuration example: 1.5.13-release.(Note that -release is part of the verison name)
   <version>{version}</version>

</dependency>
```


<span id="2a99dcc4"></span>
### Adding dependencies 2: Offline dependencies

If you don't have access to Volcano's maven repository, or don't have a jar package management tool, you can [download offline packages ](https://github.com/volcengine/datarangers-sdk-java/tree/main/jar-with-dependencies)from github, or build offline packages yourself: `mvn package -DskipTests`, the relevant jar path is:


* `datarangers-sdk-core/target/datarangers-sdk-core-{version}-release-jar-with-dependencies.jar`

* `datarangers-sdk-starter/target/datarangers-sdk-starter-{version}-release-jar-with-dependencies.jar`


<span id="2a8f2c73"></span>
## Step2: Initialize the SDK

Java development framework is usually SpringBoot framework (recommended), Spring containerization, ordinary Java program, the code structure of the three ways are different, but the initialization of the configuration parameters are consistent, the example is described below.

<span id="2b66f60f"></span>
### HTTP


* HTTP mode is simple to deploy, highly reliable, and also supports batch reporting. Therefore, it is recommended to use HTTP mode in other scenarios except for KAFKA mode reporting in the same network scenario.

* When using HTTP mode, the **SDK version requires \> = 1.5.7.** 

* When using HTTP mode, when initializing the SDK, specify which mode is currently used to report data through the `datarangers.sdk.mode`parameter, `datarangers.sdk.mode = http`means using HTTP mode.


The following are examples and configuration parameter descriptions of using HTTP mode in different environments.

<span id="d87aae93"></span>
#### SAAS\-Cloud Native


<Tabs>
<Tab zoneid="CNt8gU33A2" title="SpringBoot Framework (recommended)">
<TabTitle>SpringBoot Framework (recommended)</TabTitle>

It is recommended to use the configuration method for initialization, configure the relevant parameters in properties or yml, and then refer to the bean to report. The configuration example is as follows.

```Properties
#Set up environment information
datarangers.sdk.env=saas_native
#Configure the reporting mode
datarangers.sdk.mode=http

# [domain]
Server IP or domain name
datarangers.sdk.domain=https://gator.****.com

# [app key]
datarangers.sdk.appKeys.20000000=xxxxxxxx
```



</Tab>
<Tab zoneid="UAWRFPSJUB" title="Spring containerization">
<TabTitle>Spring containerization</TabTitle>

It is recommended that initialization operations be assembled into beans and managed by the Spring container. It can be used by injecting it into the class in use.

```XML
<!-- sdkMode config -->
<bean name="sdkMode" class="org.springframework.beans.factory.config.FieldRetrievingFactoryBean">
    <property name="staticField" value="com.datarangers.config.SdkMode.HTTP" />    
</bean>

<bean name="dataRangersSDKConfigProperties" class="com.datarangers.config.DataRangersSDKConfigProperties">
    <property name="env" ref="saas_native"/>
    <property name="domain" value="{domain}"/>
    <property name="mode" ref="sdkMode"/>
    <property name="appKeys">
      <map>
        <entry key=" \\${appId}" value=" \\${appKey}"/>
      </map>
    </property>
</bean>
```



</Tab>
<Tab zoneid="bGMUGOWIFX" title="Ordinary Java">
<TabTitle>Ordinary Java</TabTitle>

```Java
DataRangersSDKConfigProperties properties = new DataRangersSDKConfigProperties();
//setting mode
properties.setEnv(Constants.ENV_SAAS_NATIVE);
properties.setMode(SdkMode.HTTP);

//Set domain and appKey
properties.setDomain("https://gator.***.com");

//Multiple apps can be set, please replace them with real parameters.
properties.getAppKeys().put(Integer.valueOf(System.getenv("SDK_APP_1")), System.getenv("SDK_APP_KEY_1"));

//Set the server level event tracking real-time verification url
// properties.getVerify().setUrl(System.getenv("VERIFY_URL"));

//Initialize collector
appEventCollector = new AppEventCollector("app", properties);
webEventCollector = new AppEventCollector("web", properties);
```



</Tab>
</Tabs>


The core configuration parameters are described below, see more full configuration parameters [Reference: Java SDK full configuration item description](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Java_SDK_Integration#63d973a1).


|Parameter |Type |Is it required? |Configuration instructions |
|---|---|---|---|
|datarangers.sdk.env |string |Yes |Configured as: saas_native, indicating that the currently used DataFinder environment is a SaaS\-cloud native environment. |
|datarangers.sdk.mode |string |Yes |Configured as: http, indicating that data is reported using http mode. |
|datarangers.sdk.domain |string |Yes |Configure the data reporting address for your SaaS\-cloud native environment provided by DataFinder, see the above [Step 3: Obtain the data upload address](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Java_SDK_Integration#ed652ecc)section. |
|datarangers.sdk.appKeys |map |Yes |Configure the appid and appkey of the app that reports data. Configuration format for example `datarangers.sdk.appKeys.20000000 = xxxxxxxx`.<br><br>Of which:<br><br><br>* 20000000: for app_id,<br><br>* XXXXXXXX: For app_key<br><br><br>app_id and app_key can be found in the above [Step 2: Get the APPID/APP Key](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Java_SDK_Integration#ff82f708)section. |


<span id="816817c3"></span>
#### Privatization


<Tabs>
<Tab zoneid="p4sv1mqyDZ" title="SpringBoot Framework (recommended)">
<TabTitle>SpringBoot Framework (recommended)</TabTitle>

Taking the initialization configuration by using the configuration as an example, the application.properties example in the privatization scenario:

```Properties
#privatization configuration example
#Use http reporting mode
datarangers.sdk.mode=http
#SDK report address, starting with http://or https://
datarangers.sdk.domain= \\${SDK_DOMAIN}

#Number of asynchronous threads, which can be adjusted when there is not enough concurrency
#datarangers.sdk.threadCount=20

#[http config]
The unit is milliseconds
#datarangers.sdk.httpConfig.requestTimeout=10000
#datarangers.sdk.httpConfig.connectTimeout=10000
#datarangers.sdk.httpConfig.socketTimeout=20000

The unit is s.
#datarangers.sdk.httpConfig.keepAliveTimeout=30

# [batch]
#Use the batch method
# datarangers.sdk.sendBatch=false
#Number of batches
#datarangers.sdk.batchSize=20
#datarangers.sdk.waitTimeMs=100
```



</Tab>
<Tab zoneid="JUO4ZfzfzX" title="Spring containerization">
<TabTitle>Spring containerization</TabTitle>

It is recommended that initialization operations be assembled into beans and managed by the Spring container. It can be used by injecting it into the class in use.

```XML
<bean name="sdkMode" class="org.springframework.beans.factory.config.FieldRetrievingFactoryBean">
    <property name="staticField" value="com.datarangers.config.SdkMode.HTTP" />    
</bean>

<bean name="dataRangersSDKConfigProperties" class="com.datarangers.config.DataRangersSDKConfigProperties">
    <property name="domain" value="{domain}"/>
    <property name="mode" ref="sdkMode"/>
</bean>
```



</Tab>
<Tab zoneid="KoINuP1HBT" title="Ordinary Java">
<TabTitle>Ordinary Java</TabTitle>

```Java
DataRangersSDKConfigProperties properties = new DataRangersSDKConfigProperties();
//setting mode
properties.setMode(SdkMode.HTTP);

//Set the sdk domain, pay attention to replace it with real parameters here
properties.setDomain(System.getenv("SDK_DOMAIN"));

//Initialize collector
appEventCollector = new AppEventCollector("app", properties);
webEventCollector = new AppEventCollector("web", properties);
mpEventCollector = new AppEventCollector("mp", properties);
```



</Tab>
</Tabs>


The core configuration parameters are described below, see more full configuration parameters [Reference: Java SDK full configuration item description](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Java_SDK_Integration#63d973a1).


|Parameter |Type |Is it required? |Configuration instructions |
|---|---|---|---|
|datarangers.sdk.env |string |No |Privatization means privatization of the environment. In a privatized environment, you don't need to manually modify this parameter, and the SDK automatically recognizes your current environment as privatized. |
|datarangers.sdk.mode |string |Yes |Http, indicating http mode |
|datarangers.sdk.domain |string |Yes |Data reporting address, the data reporting address of the privatized environment is the data sending address that is planned and configured by itself. If you are unsure of this address, please contact your project manager or customer success manager. |


<span id="21044352"></span>
### KAFKA model (privatization only)


* The KAFKA pattern is simple to deploy, highly reliable, and has good data reporting performance. Therefore, in the privatization scenario, it is recommended to use this pattern when the service integrating the SDK and the DataFinder are on the same network.

* **The model is only supported in privatization** .

* When initializing the SDK, the `datarangers.sdk.mode`parameter specifies which mode is currently used to report data, `atarangers.sdk.mode = kafka`indicates that the KAFKA mode is used.



<Tabs>
<Tab zoneid="AJapPeZV2m" title="SpringBoot Framework (recommended)">
<TabTitle>SpringBoot Framework (recommended)</TabTitle>

Taking the initialization configuration by using the configuration as an example, the application.properties example in the privatization scenario:

```Properties
#privatization configuration example
#Use the mode reported by Kafka
datarangers.sdk.mode=kafka
datarangers.sdk.kafka.bootstrapServers={ip1}:9192,{ip2}:9192

#Kafka producer properties can be configured here
#datarangers.sdk.kafka.properties.retries=3
```


Note: If the property's key contains. Special characters need to be included with [], such as:


* properties：

   ```Properties
   #Use the mode reported by Kafka
   datarangers.sdk.mode=kafka
   datarangers.sdk.kafka.bootstrapServers={ip1}:9192,{ip2}:9192
   
   #Kafka producer properties can be configured here
   #datarangers.sdk.kafka.properties.retries=3
   datarangers.sdk.kafka.properties."[sasl.mechanisms]"=PLAIN
   datarangers.sdk.kafka.properties."[security.protocol]"=SASL_PLAINTEXT
   datarangers.sdk.kafka.properties."[sasl.jaas.config]"=;
   datarangers.sdk.kafka.properties."[sasl.kerberos.service.name]"=kafka
   ```
   

* yml：

   ```YAML
   datarangers:
    sdk:
      mode: kafka
      kafka:
       bootstrapServers: {ip1}:9192,{ip2}:9192
       properties:
         "[sasl.mechanism]": GSSAPI
         "[security.protocol]": SASL_PLAINTEXT
         "[sasl.jaas.config]": ''
         "[sasl.kerberos.service.name]": kafka
   ```
   


</Tab>
<Tab zoneid="IJN7Qrmcx3" title="Spring containerization">
<TabTitle>Spring containerization</TabTitle>

It is recommended that initialization operations be assembled into beans and managed by the Spring container. It can be used by injecting it into the class in use.

```XML
<bean name="sdkMode" class="org.springframework.beans.factory.config.FieldRetrievingFactoryBean">
    <property name="staticField" value="com.datarangers.config.SdkMode.KAFKA" />    
</bean>

<bean name="kafakConfig" class="com.datarangers.config.KafkaConfig">
    <property name="bootstrapServers" value=" \\${ip:port}" />
    <property name="properties">
      <map>
        <entry key=" \\${key}" value=" \\${value}"/>
      </map>
    </property>
</bean>

<bean name="dataRangersSDKConfigProperties" class="com.datarangers.config.DataRangersSDKConfigProperties">
    <property name="mode" ref="sdkMode"/>
</bean>
```



</Tab>
<Tab zoneid="oar7pvbvYH" title="Ordinary Java">
<TabTitle>Ordinary Java</TabTitle>

```Java
DataRangersSDKConfigProperties properties = new DataRangersSDKConfigProperties();

//setting mode
properties.setMode(SdkMode.KAFKA);

//set up kafka
KafkaConfig kafkaConfig = new KafkaConfig();
properties.setKafka(kafkaConfig);

//Set BootstrapServers, etc: 127.0.0.1:9192, localhost:9192, pay attention to replace it with real parameters here
String bootstrapServers = System.getenv("SDK_KAFKA_BOOTSTRAP_SERVERS");
if(bootstrapServers == null){
    throw new IllegalArgumentException("bootstrapServers can not be empty");
}
kafkaConfig.setBootstrapServers(bootstrapServers);

//If you need to set other properties, you can set them.
// Map<String, Object> kafkaProperties = new HashMap<>();
// kafkaConfig.setProperties(kafkaProperties);

//Initialize collector
webEventCollector = new AppEventCollector("web", properties);
mpEventCollector = new AppEventCollector("mp", properties);
appEventCollector = new AppEventCollector("app", properties);
```



</Tab>
</Tabs>


The core configuration parameters are described below, see more full configuration parameters [Reference: Java SDK full configuration item description](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Java_SDK_Integration#63d973a1).


|Parameter |Type |Is it required? |Sample value |
|---|---|---|---|
|datarangers.sdk.env |string |No |Privatization means privatization of the environment. In a privatized environment, you don't need to manually modify this parameter, and the SDK automatically recognizes your current environment as privatized. |
|datarangers.sdk.mode |string |Yes |Kafka, which represents the Kafka pattern |
|datarangers.sdk.kafka.bootstrapServers |string |Yes |Kafka's bootstrapServers address: `{ip1}: 9192, {ip2}: 9192` |
|datarangers.sdk.kafka.properties |map |No |Other kafka parameter configuration, you can use the form of `datarangers.sdk.kafka.properties.xxx = xxx`configuration, kafkaProducer parameter reference: [Kafka official website documentation ](https://kafka.apache.org/0102/documentation.html#producerconfigs).<br><br>Configuration example: `datarangers.sdk.kafka.properties retries = 3` |


<span id="c55dc425"></span>
## Verify the integration configuration

<span id="2ad6edcc"></span>
### View startup log

Startup prints the following log, which can be monitored to determine if the configuration is as expected. Mainly focus on `env`, `sdkMode`, `domain`and other configurations.

```Plain
sdk config properties: 
enable: true 
env: PRIVATIZATION 
sync: false 
sdkMode: HTTP  
domain: ...
headers: {...}  
threadCount: 20 
queueSize: 10240 
sendBatch: false 
batchSize: 20 
waitTimeMs: 100 
httpConfig: {...} 
eventSavePath: logs/ 
eventSaveName: datarangers.log 
eventFilePaths: [logs/] 
eventSaveMaxFileSize: 100 
eventSaveMaxDays: -1 
openapiConfig: {...} 
kafka: null
```


<span id="f28d46fd"></span>
### HTTP Mode Debug Verification


* Check the configuration or automatic log to make sure the configured `sdkMode`is `HTTP`and check:

   * Check whether the datarangers.log file has data. If there is event tracking data, it is an exception (because in HTTP mode, the file will not have data). Please check the set sdkMode effective value.

   * Check the error\-datarangers.log file, and check for error messages if there is data present

* Debug Validation Request/Response Messages

   If you can't determine what the exception is through the log, you can use debug to see the detailed error information, Debug breakpoint HttpUtils class 167 lines (different versions may have different lines, but the logic is to get the request and response message), the following screenshot is 1.5.3 version.

   <span>![图片](https://p9-arcosite.byteimg.com/tos-cn-i-goo7wpa0wc/e1978c482d464ef8a24ac0314154ef93~tplv-goo7wpa0wc-image.image) </span>

   * ResustStr is a response message, where if e is not 0, it means that the report failed, otherwise it means that the report was successful.

   * Body request message, if the response message to learn the error, you can get down to see if the data format is correct.


<span id="cb0790c1"></span>
### HTTP mode curl authentication

You can use the curl command to see if it can be reported normally. The following are validation examples for each environment.

<div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="warning" data-tips-is-title="true">warning</div>


<div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="warning">You need to change the <code>local_time_ms</code>and <code>datetime</code>fields in the script to the current time.</div>


<span id="39d6ceeb"></span>
#### SaaS\-cloud native environment

The appkey needs to be replaced with the corresponding configuration.

```Bash
curl --location --request POST 'https://gator.volces.com/sdk/log' \
--header 'User-Agent: DataRangers Java SDK' \
--header 'X-MCS-AppKey:  \${AppKey}' \
--header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
--data '{
    "app_type": "app",
    "_format_name": "datarangers_svc_app_log_v3_server_sdk_1.2.7",
    "header": {
        "custom": {
            "client": "fdaf",
            "__sdk_platform": "datarangers_sdk"
        },
        "device_id": 0,
        "timezone": 8,
        "tz_offset": 28800,
        "tz_name": "Asia/Shanghai",
        "user_unique_id": "test_sdk_user"
    },
    "user_unique_id": "xxxx",
    "event_v3": [
        {
            "event": "补贴查询",
            "params": {
                "cardNum": "cardNum",
                "year": "2021"
            },
            "local_time_ms": 1637734994778,
            "datetime": "2021-12-15 14:23:14"
        }
    ]
}'
```


The following return indicates successful reporting:

```JSON
{
    "e":0,
    "magic_tag":"server_sdk_log",
    "message":"success",
    "server_time":1664352669
}
```

<span id="3fb39cdd"></span>
# Event tracking report

<span id="d6d1310f"></span>
## Precautions

The current SaaS cloud\-native and privatization scenarios do not have the same reporting methods in user properties, item properties, and other reporting scenarios. You need to first understand the data reporting precautions for the corresponding environment according to the actual use environment.


|Subdivision |SaaS\-Cloud Native/Privatized |
|---|---|
|Normal Event Property |Just call sendEvent, and use the parameters in sendEvent to flexibly set the property type and other parameters of the reported event properties. |
|user properties |* When reporting the device information of the user such as client_ip, device_model obtained by the server level, you need to call sendEvent and report it through the header interface parameters.<br><br>* Otherwise, by default, the public properties for the event are either null or unknown. |
|Item Properties |The Item property needs to be created in the system before being reported. The currently supported reporting methods are:<br><br><br>* Offline upload: Support uploading offline Item attribute files in CSV format. After uploading, complete the association between Item attribute and Item dimension on the metadata management \> business dimension interface. Please refer to the details [Business Dimension (Item) Data Access (Local File Upload)](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Business_Dimension_Item_Data_Access_Local_File_Upload).<br><br>* HTTP reporting: The Item property is reported using the HTTP API, see [6. Report business object properties](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/HTTP_API#_6-%E4%B8%8A%E6%8A%A5%E4%B8%9A%E5%8A%A1%E5%AF%B9%E8%B1%A1%E5%B1%9E%E6%80%A7).<br><br><br>See more guidance on business dimension access [Business Dimension (Item) Data Access and Usage Practices](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Business_Dimension_Item_Data_Access_and_Usage_Practices). |


<span id="ba0a5c96"></span>
## Send normal events

An event can be reported by calling the `sendEvent`API of the Java SDK.

```Java
@Resource(name = "appEventCollector")
private EventCollector appEventCollector;

appEventCollector.sendEvent("uuid2", 10000000, null, "test_event_java_sdk", new HashMap<String, Object>() {{
    put("date_time", LocalDateTime.now().format(DateTimeFormatter.ofPattern("yyyyMMdd")));
    put("current_time", LocalDateTime.now().format(DateTimeFormatter.ofPattern("yyyyMMdd HH:mm:ss")));
}});
```



* The above is an example of reporting. The `sendEvent`API has multiple interface definitions, which can be flexibly configured to report events. Please refer to the details [sendEvent](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Java_SDK_API_Description#8c953840).

* If you want to report events in bulk, you can use the `sendEvents`API, see details [sendEvents](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Java_SDK_API_Description#6f9e6525).


<span id="ae5733a3"></span>
## Set user properties

User properties need to be created in the system before reporting. When reporting, you can call the user properties setting related API of the Java SDK to set user properties. The example is as follows.

```Java
eventCollector.profileSet("uuid-1", 10000028, new HashMap<String, Object>() {{
    put("profile_1", "param_1");
    put("profile_2", "param_2");
    put("profile_3", "param_3");
    put("profile_4", "param_4");
}});
```



* For more API details on user property settings, see [user property related interface](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Java_SDK_API_Description#953bdc03).


<span id="76844241"></span>
## Set Item Properties

The Item property needs to be created in the system before being reported. The built\-in id attribute of the business object, the corresponding field name is called item_id, so there is no need to define an `id`attribute.

<div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="warning" data-tips-is-title="true">warning</div>


<div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="warning">If you create a business object (Item), the <strong>business object name</strong> ( <strong>property name</strong> ) is named in the hump way, it will be automatically converted to underscore format when reporting with the Java SDK. For example, you create a business object named <strong>FirstName</strong> that is converted to a <strong>First_Name</strong> when the data is reported. If you want to preserve the hump format, you can instead use the HTTP API to report the data.</div>


Here is an example of setting the Item property.

```Java
List<Item> items = new ArrayList<>();
items.add(new BookItem("1000", "book").setName("Java").setPrice(100).setPublishDate(LocalDate.now()).setAuthors(author).setCategory("computer"));
items.add(new BookItem("1002", "book").setName("PHP").setPrice(100).setPublishDate(LocalDate.now()).setAuthors(author).setCategory("computer"));
eventCollector.itemSet(10000028, "book", items);
```



* See more API details for Item property settings [business object related interface](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Java_SDK_API_Description#1f822ab0).


<span id="ca7860bc"></span>
## Send events carrying items

```Java
List<Item> items = new ArrayList<>();
items.add(new BookItem("1000", "book"));
items.add(new BookItem("1002", "book"));
items.add(new PhoneItem("1002", "phone"));
eventCollector.sendEvent("user-001", 10000028, null, "set_items", new HashMap<String, Object>() {{
    put("param1", "params");
    put("param2", items.get(0));
    put("param3", items.get(1));
    put("param4", items.get(2));
}});
```


<span id="7841b0a0"></span>
## Reporting anonymous user events

If you need to use the server to report anonymous user event information, you need to set the value of the user_unique_id to " (empty string), and then set other device information that can be associated, such as device_id, web_id, anonymousId. If the user logs in, can get user_unique_id, and want to log in after the real name behavior can be associated with the behavior before anonymity, then after setting the correct user_unique_id, but also need to bring the time set anonymous device_id, web_id or anonymousId.

<span id="e912c613"></span>
### Use device_id/web_id to report anonymous user events

When using `appEventCollector`, deviceId is device_id, when using `webEventCollector`, `mpEventCollector`, deviceId is web_id.

```Java
Map<String, Object> eventParams = new HashMap<>();
eventParams.put("date_time", new SimpleDateFormat("yyyyMMdd").format(new Date()));
eventParams.put("event_param1", "value1");

//app/web/mp are all deviceId here.
Long deviceId = 10000L;
Header header = new HeaderV3.Builder()
        .setAppId(appId)
        .setDeviceId(deviceId)
        .setUserUniqueId("")
        .build();

//app/web/mp3 Use different EventCollectors
// app
appEventCollector.sendEvent(header,"test_app_event_anonymous", eventParams, System.currentTimeMillis());

//After the real name, associate the anonymous behavior, u1 will associate the anonymous user behavior set before (associate according to deviceId)
Header header2 = new HeaderV3.Builder()
        .setAppId(appId)
        .setDeviceId(deviceId)
        .setUserUniqueId("u1")
        .build();
appEventCollector.sendEvent(header2,"test_app_event_anonymous", eventParams, System.currentTimeMillis());

// web
webEventCollector.sendEvent(header,"test_web_event_anonymous", eventParams, System.currentTimeMillis());

// mp
mpEventCollector.sendEvent(header,"test_mp_event_anonymous", eventParams, System.currentTimeMillis());
```


<span id="87fb42ed"></span>
### Use anonymousId to report anonymous user events

User device_id/web_id are long type, if the user's custom anonymous ID is string, then device_id/web_id can not be satisfied, you can use anonymousId string type field to report.

AnonymousId only supports web/mp, that is, to use webEventCollector or mpEventCollector to report.

```Java
Map<String, Object> eventParams = new HashMap<>();
eventParams.put("date_time", new SimpleDateFormat("yyyyMMdd").format(new Date()));
eventParams.put("event_param1", "value1");

String anonymousId="test_anonymousId1";
Header header = new HeaderV3.Builder()
        .setAppId(appId)
        .setAnonymousId(anonymousId)
        .setUserUniqueId("")
        .build();
// web
webEventCollector.sendEvent(header,"test_web_event_anonymous", eventParams, System.currentTimeMillis());

//After the real name, associate the anonymous behavior, u1 will associate the anonymous user behavior set before (associate according to anonymousId)
Header header2 = new HeaderV3.Builder()
        .setAppId(appId)
        .setAnonymousId(anonymousId)
        .setUserUniqueId("u1")
        .build();
webEventCollector.sendEvent(header2,"test_web_event_anonymous", eventParams, System.currentTimeMillis());

// mp
mpEventCollector.sendEvent(header,"test_mp_event_anonymous", eventParams, System.currentTimeMillis());
```


<span id="45a7101e"></span>
## Report historical data

**Note: The [SaaS\-cloud\-native] and [privatization] versions can be viewed in real time.** 

If the client side time of the data exceeds seven days, it cannot be imported under normal circumstances. If you need to import historical data, you need to add the identity `__is_history`of the historical data in the `custom`field of the `header`, and the attribute value is set to string `"true"`.

The code example is as follows:

```Java
appEventCollector.sendEvent(userUniqueId, appId, new HashMap<String, Object>() {{
                    put("__is_history","true");
                }}, "test_event",
                new HashMap<String, Object>() {{
                    put("date_time", new SimpleDateFormat("yyyyMMdd").format(new Date()));
                    put("current_time",
                            new SimpleDateFormat("yyyyMMdd HH:mm:ss").format(new Date()));
                }},
                1637734994778);
```


<span id="95a83ff0"></span>
# Validate event tracking data

Verify the metadata first, and then check it in the behavioral scrutiny.

<span>![图片](https://p9-arcosite.byteimg.com/tos-cn-i-goo7wpa0wc/ef1e842377504022ad21d20e395d3c0a~tplv-goo7wpa0wc-image.image) </span>

<span id="6e276494"></span>
## Validation event

After the event is successfully sent, if it is reported for the first time in a new event, it may take up to 5 minutes to check. First check whether the metadata is normal:


* Check if there are any reported events under "Data Management" \> "Metadata Management" \> "General Events".

* Under "Data Management" \> "Metadata Management" \> "Event Properties", check whether there are reported properties, and whether the type of attribute and the event associated with the attribute are correct.


When the event exists in the metadata, it can be directly checked by the user.

<span id="7e4bb7c2"></span>
## Verify user properties

(1) First verify whether the user attribute exists in "Data Management" \> "Metadata Management" \> "User Properties", and check whether the attribute type meets expectations.

(2) Then in "Analysis Tools" \> "User Analysis" \> "User Detail", click and enter one of the user details pages to view the recently reported user properties.


* After the user properties are reported, you can view the corresponding user properties in the most recent profile of the user.

   <span>![图片](https://p9-arcosite.byteimg.com/tos-cn-i-goo7wpa0wc/a52d90ee2e4043c7b3ad15c6b98eaf49~tplv-goo7wpa0wc-image.image) </span>

* After events related to user properties are also reported synchronously, you can view the corresponding user properties in the public properties list at the bottom right.

   However, after reporting user properties, be sure to report an event, otherwise the user may not be able to find the public property list here, because user scrutiny is associated with the event.

   <span>![图片](https://p9-arcosite.byteimg.com/tos-cn-i-goo7wpa0wc/651d53f6ae3c4dc9b8743a27ae405041~tplv-goo7wpa0wc-image.image) </span>


<span id="303a590e"></span>
## Validate business object

First check whether the business object is bound to the event under "Data Management" \> "Business Objects". Then you can query in the behavior review, and the item_id will be displayed in the behavior review.

<span>![图片](https://p9-arcosite.byteimg.com/tos-cn-i-goo7wpa0wc/425b90b6ab2f4e1f84428f0e95fe83f2~tplv-goo7wpa0wc-image.image) </span>

If you want to view the property values of business objects, you can check them in "Analysis Tools" \> "Advanced Analysis" \> "Business Object Analysis".

<span id="a3a72c61"></span>
## Real\-time event tracking

Select "server level event tracking" on "Data Management" \> "General Events" \> "Verification Event Tracking", then enter the user_unique_id to be detected, and then set the url parameter to verified.url.

<span>![图片](https://p9-arcosite.byteimg.com/tos-cn-i-goo7wpa0wc/785b3e7e2d01467480f3e8f2362ed1e5~tplv-goo7wpa0wc-image.image) </span>

When the user's event tracking data is reported, you will see the reported content data.

<span>![图片](https://p9-arcosite.byteimg.com/tos-cn-i-goo7wpa0wc/9f47843cbd9c415ebdb118512fef676b~tplv-goo7wpa0wc-image.image) </span>


1. Note that the URL valid period is only **60 minutes**.

2. **SDK version \> = 1.5.7**.

3. If the URL is wrong or expired, the real\-time detection will not be reported or failed, but it will not affect the normal event tracking report.

4. If you can't view the content data on the page, you can check the log of the real\-time event tracking report first:

   1. Search for the keywords ERROR logs, as well as "verify request" and "verify config".

   2. The related class reported in real time is `com.datarangers.sender. VerifySender`, which can be debugged.

   3. There is no error log, but the real\-time report does not display the content. You can refresh the next page to regenerate the URL.


<span id="f8a5c9b7"></span>
## Precautions

If the data cannot be found on the page, you can try to refresh the page.

<span id="63d973a1"></span>
# Reference: Java SDK full configuration item description

AppEventCollector uses two parameters: appType and properties.


* appType only supports:

   * App, upload data related to the mobile end of the application at the server level

   * Web, upload data related to the web side of the application at the server level

   * MP, upload data related to the application Mini Program at the server level

* The properties prefix is `datarangers.sdk`.



|Configuration module |Configuration item |Meaning |Remarks |
|---|---|---|---|
|Does not involve |mode |Reporting mode (case insensitive): http, file, kafka |After the Java SDK version \> = 1.5.7 version, it is recommended to use the new configuration. When mode and save coexist, mode shall prevail. |
||env |Enumeration type, saas means cloud, privatization means privatization, not necessary, SDK can automatically determine according to the configuration. |without |
||sync |Boolean type, synchronous asynchronous, default to false, using asynchronous reporting. |without |
||save |Boolean variable, indicating whether to save to a local file, saas only supports configuration to false. |This configuration is deprecated after the \> = 1.5.7 version, using the `mode`configuration. |
|http |domain |DataFinder's domain name or ip, supports http and https, for example **https://{specific domain address}**  .<br><br>In a SaaS environment, you need to modify it to the corresponding domain name:<br><br><br>* SaaS\-Cloud Native: [https://gator.volces.com](https://gator.volces.com/) |When using HTTP reporting mode, it must be configured. |
||threadCount |In the number of core threads in the asynchronous thread pool, the default is 20. |without |
||httpConfig.requestTimeout |The request timed out by HTTP is in milliseconds, the default is 10000. |without |
||httpConfig.connectTimeout |The connection timeout sent by http is in milliseconds, and the default is 10000. |without |
||httpConfig.socketTimeout |The socket timeout sent by http is in milliseconds, and the default is 20000. |without |
||httpConfig.keepAliveTimeout |The keepAliveTimeout of the http connection pool, in seconds, defaults to 30. |without |
||httpConfig.trustDisable |true/false。 Whether to disable two\-way authentication. If an SSL\-related error occurs, it is recommended to configure the certificate first, or configure it to true to disable two\-way authentication. Default is true |without |
||httpConfig.customKeyTrustEnable |True indicates the certificate path and password of the custom client, the default is false |without |
||httpConfig.keyMaterialPath |keyMaterial path |without |
||httpConfig.keyPassword |Key Password |without |
||httpConfig.storePassword |Store password |without |
||httpConfig.trustMaterialPath |trustMaterial path |without |
||httpConfig.trustStrategy |Trust strategy.<br><br><br>* Self, self\-signed policy<br><br>* All, trust all | |
||sendBatch |Boolean type, indicating whether to enable bulk reporting. Default is false, do not use batch. |Environments support bulk reporting starting with 1.5.7 versions (inclusive). |
||batchSize |Number of batch reports | |
||waitTimeMs |Batch report, when the batchSize is insufficient, the maximum waiting time | |
||appKeys.$ |SAAS environment, report the set appkeys, multiple can be set. Several possible ways are:<br><br>`yaml <br> datarangers.sdk.appKeys.${APP_ID_1}=${APP_KEY_1} <br> datarangers.sdk.appKeys.${APP_ID_2}=${APP_KEY_2} <br>` |Be careful to replace with real app_id and appkey. |
||eventCountFileDisable |Indicates whether to disable the count.log file, the default is false; set to true, there will be no count.log | |
|http（OpenAPI） |openapiConfig.ak |OpenAPI ak, please contact the account manager to obtain. | |
||openapiConfig.sk |OpenAPI sk, please contact the account manager to obtain. | |
|file |eventSaveName |The file name to save the log, you need to ensure the write permission of the file, the default is datarangers.log. |without |
||eventSavePath |The file path to save the log, you need to ensure write permission and create file permission, the mode is logs/ |without |
||eventSaveMaxFileSize |Represents the maximum file size of the log file to be saved, in MB, with a default of 100. |without |
||eventCountFileDisable |Indicates whether to disable the count.log file, the default is false; set to true, there will be no count.log | |
||eventFilePaths |Represents the location of the log file that needs to be saved, as a string array, each value in the array represents a path, and the user writes the log file to a different folder, which can be used with multiple LogAgent instances.<br><br>If the array is defined, eventSavePath will not take effect. |without |
||eventSaveMaxDays |The maximum number of days to keep the log file, beyond this time the log will be deleted, the default is \-1, that is, do not delete the file. Therefore, when running for a long time, in order to avoid taking up too much disk, you need to delete the log file yourself, or configure a reasonable value, such as 7. |without |
|kafka |bootstrapServers |The address of Kafka. |Configuration is required to use the Kafka pattern. |
||properties |Is a map, other Kafka properties that need to be configured. Parameter reference of kafkaProducer: [Kafka official website documentation](https://kafka.apache.org/0102/documentation.html#producerconfigs) | |
|verify |verify.url |Server level event tracking url address detected in real time. |**SDK version \> = 1.5.7** |
